tasks.title: aosa status must survive an unreadable budget.json
tasks.why: aosa.py:245-247 ([A11], new) turns a corrupt budget.json into die(), which raises SystemExit. cmd_status calls load_budget inside 'try: ... except Exception' (418-422) and main wraps status in 'except Exception' (1654-1658), and SystemExit is not an Exception: so one truncated budget.json makes `aosa.py status` exit 1 and stop printing at the budget line - the backlog counts and the mode P/E/B line the loop reads every cycle never appear, against the documented 'status always exits 0'. test_a11_unreadable_budget_is_not_reset only exercises the `budget` command, so nothing catches it. P2.
tasks.done_when: a test in Tools/aosa/test_aosa.py writes a truncated budget.json, runs `status`, and asserts exit 0 with both 'budget : unreadable' and a 'mode   :' line in the output; red on today's code

tasks.title: write budget.json and BACKLOG.md atomically, as LEDGER.md is
tasks.why: [A14] gave LEDGER.md write_atomic (aosa.py:103-114, 1283), but the loop's other records are still plain write_text: budget.json at 242, 1194 and 1215 (the money record: the daily cap and every entry) and BACKLOG.md at 1127, where cmd_age rewrites the whole card table in place. A process killed or a disk full mid-write leaves a half file; for budget.json that is now fatal by design ([A11] refuses to read it), so the loop stops until a human repairs it, and every past charge is lost. The helper is already in the file. P2.
tasks.done_when: a test patches aosa.os.replace to raise, calls `age` and the budget writer, and asserts the old budget.json and BACKLOG.md are byte-identical afterwards with no .tmp left behind (the shape of test_a14_a_failed_ledger_write_keeps_the_old_file); red on today's code

tasks.title: abtest: stop when editor_lock wait timed out
tasks.why: abtest.py:61 and :177 run `editor_lock.py wait --timeout 3600` with check=False and never read the return code, and editor_lock's wait branch returns 1 when the lock is still held. So after an hour of silent waiting abtest starts a batch editor on a project another editor already has open: Unity refuses the project, no results XML is written, run_tests returns None, and the user is told 'no verdict (compile error? see the log)' - the one reason it was not. fails-on-old then exits with that same wrong reason, after swapping production files over the tree and burning two hours. P2.
tasks.done_when: a python test runs abtest with a stand-in editor_lock.py that exits 1 and asserts abtest exits non-zero naming the held lock, and never launches the editor stand-in; red on today's code

tasks.title: land.ps1 must read prune --apply's new exit code
tasks.why: aosa/land.ps1:106 pipes `aosa.py prune --apply` into the log and never checks $LASTEXITCODE, but [A17] (aosa.py:1419-1430) just gave prune exit 1 for every item it could not delete. A snapshot held open by a running player therefore stays on disk, the line scrolls past in the log, and land.ps1 still prints 'OK: gate green' and exits 0 - against its own header, 'Exit 0 = everything asked for passed'. The retention rule exists because cycle 8 found 4.5 GB of unread copies, so the one signal that it did not run has no reader. P3.
tasks.done_when: a Tools/selftest.py case runs land.ps1 -EditOnly with its stand-ins and a prune that exits 1, and asserts land.ps1 exits non-zero and the log says the retention rule did not finish; red on today's land.ps1
